headline: High: shared writable workspace plus broad tool access creates prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk; no critical compliance mismatch is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers and can propose edits; LangGraph can ingest developer-defined tool outputs and stdin/stdout in graph workflows. With a shared workspace or copied outputs, malicious content from one can steer the other. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, but no direct default bridge is shown.
conditions: IF Copilot outputs are pasted into a LangGraph prompt or node input, injection becomes plausible.
IF LangGraph forwards tool output into a Copilot-visible file or buffer, Copilot may treat it as trusted text.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Require a human review step before copying outputs between agents.
Prefix all inter-agent text with provenance labels.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files into prompts.
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, while LangGraph can read application-defined files and send data to model providers or developer-defined tools. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or state can flow from one agent into the other and then out to external APIs. The profiles do not prove a default shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory, file contents can be exposed across the pair.
IF LangGraph nodes send shared state to model providers, copied code or secrets may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate repos or directories.
Remove secrets from shared files before orchestration.
Restrict LangGraph nodes to minimal state.
Audit outbound prompts for code and credentials.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; LangGraph can also write the filesystem and run subprocesses with broad egress. In a shared checkout, concurrent edits or git mutations can race and overwrite each other. The profiles show overlapping write authority, but not unrestricted same-dir locking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git working tree, concurrent changes can conflict.
IF LangGraph subprocesses edit files that Copilot also proposes edits for, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize write operations with a lock file.
Review diffs before applying edits.
Limit LangGraph to read-only mode during Copilot sessions.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces code suggestions and Workspace edits, and LangGraph is a general orchestration layer that can act on upstream outputs via tools or nodes. If LangGraph treats Copilot-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated actions or commits. Because the pair can combine suggestion generation with action-taking, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF LangGraph consumes Copilot-generated code or instructions without verification, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF LangGraph nodes execute or deploy based on Copilot output, a single hallucination can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any action.
Require tests to pass before execution.
Keep Copilot output advisory only.
Log and diff all upstream text before use.
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action-taking nodes.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and editor buffers, while LangGraph handles application-defined graph state and model-provider API keys. If regulated data is placed into shared state, retention and residency policies may diverge across the pair. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in LangGraph state while Copilot indexes the same repository, retention controls may diverge.
IF the shared workflow includes EU PII or PHI, policy review is required before use.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts or state.
Review vendor retention settings for both services.
Separate compliance-sensitive projects from general coding tasks.
Document data flows for the workflow.
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware routing and retention controls.
